patch.value: Implement native item file doc and test collections with oracle parity
Match collection list, add and remove receipts, canonical item and append-only history bytes, refusal semantics and serialized native writers against the locked oracle.

value.author: codex-agent
value.text: Plan: route collection edits through the existing per-item lock and journal, compare complete item and append-only history bytes at a fixed clock, and prove two concurrent writers preserve accepted additions. Match collection parsing, compact receipts and typed refusals.

value.author: codex-agent
value.text: Implemented collection list and transactional add/remove paths. The first differential run exposed optional artifact note visitation in canonical history patch ordering; item hashes already agreed, but patch order and record hashes differed. Added the missing normalized-row ordering behavior before continuing exact artifact comparisons.

value.author: codex-agent
value.text: Concurrency differential passed for native and oracle writers: both additions survive, adjacent document hashes chain, and complete item/history artifacts equal serial oracle replay in observed commit order. Expanded parser checks now include Markdown pairs, quoted commas, command aliases and documentation references. Oracle artifact collections have path selectors only; linked tests additionally expose 1-based indices.

Restored exact source bytes after each control; all 169 library tests passed. The current instrumented differential run passed all 6 tests.

value.author: codex-agent

value.author: codex-agent
value.text: The complete collection-filtered linked run passed all six suites on Node 26, including agent attribution and bounded local probes. Restored source passed all nine oracle scenarios. Focused probe coverage now measures 100 percent across all four required dimensions.

value.author: codex-agent
value.text: The final full run passed all 372 tests in both phases. Coverage selected the SDK collection transaction instantiation and exposed its untested docs_add region; a real SDK docs mutation now asserts the row count and appended operation. All new production modules already met the unchanged branch floor. A fresh full release gate follows.

value.author: codex-agent
value.text: A full instrumented run exposed a real concurrent lost-update pattern: both additions used the original before-hash. Inspection found native lock initialization did not hold the cleanup gate, so minimal-governance stale recovery could steal an unpublished payload. Acquisition now gates initialization and stale reclamation together, as the oracle does. All 181 library tests pass. Behavioral revert proof: reverting only acquire_lock_attempt to its original body fails mutation::tests::initialization_gate_protects_a_lock_before_its_payload_is_published with exit 101; exact restoration passes. Twenty earlier isolated concurrency attempts passed, showing why the deterministic publication-boundary regression is necessary.

value.author: codex-agent
value.text: Final lock preflight passes: 181 library tests; deny-warnings clippy; every branch and region of initialization, reclamation and shared platform contention classification covered. The strengthened concurrency acceptance passes eight native writer pairs plus one oracle pair with the same 5-second wait and exact serial artifact replay. Linked collection tests (six differential suites plus the deterministic initialization regression) and the linked claim-next test also passed after the initialization fix. A clean full release gate now follows.

value.author: codex-agent
value.text: Final clean release-check PASS: 374 normal and 374 instrumented tests, all four source coverage dimensions exactly 100 percent (8802 lines, 852 functions, 13744 regions, 2132 branches). All 12 search/collection differential suites pass in both phases, including eight concurrent native pairs and one concurrent oracle pair with complete serial artifact replay. Merge, optional-note ordering, attribution, local-probe and lock-initialization behavioral revert proofs are recorded above. Linked collection evidence also passed (six differential suites plus the initialization regression). Audit retains only the existing allowed unsafe-libyaml maintenance warning. Feature remains in progress for review; claims are released and platform CI follows.

value.author: codex-agent
value.text: PR platform run: all three standalone OS jobs pass, and the macOS aggregate passes. The Windows aggregate passes every test and has 100 percent lines/functions/regions, but branch coverage is 2135/2136. The remaining branch is the fallback colon-reference classification in src/collections.rs:234 because absolute drive paths satisfy the first condition on Windows. Adding a real project-relative numeric-colon reference to parser and oracle fixtures covers that distinct classification without changing production behavior or any floor.

value.author: codex-agent
value.text: Windows coverage follow-up validation: fmt, deny-warnings clippy, the pair-form parser unit test and linked pm test execution all pass. The latter includes six differential suites and the deterministic initialization regression; the new numeric-colon reference is compared in both JSON and TOON with complete item/history artifacts. Production source bytes are unchanged from the passing 374-test local aggregate. The first platform run finished with five of six OS jobs passing; the single Windows branch-floor gap is the only failure. The test fixture correction now receives a fresh full three-OS run. Claim released for review; Feature remains in progress.

value.author: codex-agent
value.text: Round 2: inspecting pinned oracle gate identity checks and replacing stale gate removal with identity-checked reclamation; adding a controlled concurrency regression and behavioral revert proof.

value.author: codex-agent
value.text: Pinned oracle releases gates by owner token but stale cleanup still removes by pathname after age/process checks. Rust now claims a nested directory, rechecks observed filesystem identity while replacement is blocked, and renames the claimed gate to a unique tombstone before cleanup. No fresh shared-path gate is deleted.

value.author: codex-agent
value.text: Refined the reclamation guard to a permanent per-item advisory lease file. Rust 1.90 supports File::try_lock; the kernel releases it on crash, avoiding an abandoned nested claim. All native gate creation/reclamation/release runs under this lease. The identity check and tombstone removal remain, and the regression also verifies contention with a held lease.

value.author: codex-agent
value.text: Behavioral revert proof: reverting only reclaim_stale_gate to the original pathname remove_dir behavior makes stale_gate_reclamation_preserves_a_concurrent_replacement fail (exit 101, 0 passed, 1 failed): stale observer reclaimed a replacement gate, and the concurrent owner detects its fresh gate was deleted. Fixed implementation restored.

value.author: codex-agent
value.text: Final safety review also preserves nonempty gates in place, including ownership evidence written by another runtime. The concurrency regression checks fresh replacement identity, active advisory lease contention, missing identity, and nonempty-gate preservation. The documented serialization guarantee covers native writers; the pinned oracle does not participate in the native advisory lease.

value.author: codex-agent
value.text: The aggregate gate exposed an introduced advisory-lease release race: repeated mutation-suite runs reproduced transient LockConflict between sequential requests while other threads spawned children. Added GateLease Drop to explicitly unlock before closing, because a briefly inherited file description can outlive its parent descriptor. The existing gate regression now retains a cloned description while a successor acquires the lease. Focused gate tests and the mutation suite pass; repeated complete mutation runs and an explicit-unlock negative control are next.

value.author: codex-agent
value.text: Explicit lease release verification: 30 consecutive complete mutation_contract suite runs passed (870 tests) after GateLease unlock-before-close. The same suite reproduced the old transient LockConflict on runs 15 and 4 during diagnosis. Focused initialization/replacement gate tests pass (2/2). Running the inherited-description negative control and targeted coverage preflight before the aggregate retry.

value.author: codex-agent
value.text: The explicit-unlock behavioral negative control also fails deterministically: reverting only GateLease Drop to close-without-unlock makes stale_gate_reclamation_preserves_a_concurrent_replacement fail with LockConflict while the inherited description remains alive (exit 101, 0 passed, 1 failed). Restored the fixed Drop afterward.

value.author: codex-agent

Each fails 0 passed/1 failed with exit 101; fixed source restored. Strict clippy passes. Aggregate retry now runs on frozen source.
